findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered without a React key in the filtered rules list
findings.body: In the `origin === 'grafana'` branch of the rules map, `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` is returned without `key={key}`, while the previous code passed `key={key}` to `GrafanaRuleLoader` and the sibling branches (`datasource`, `default`) still pass their keys. The component computes a stable `key` per rule precisely to avoid key duplication in this list. Rendering list children without keys triggers React's missing-key warning and, more importantly, can mis-associate component state (e.g. the delete modal / silence drawer state held by `RuleActionsButtons`) with the wrong rule row when pages are appended or the list is re-rendered. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` element.

findings.title: Delete menu item can never appear in the rule list because it still requires a rulerRule
findings.body: The Delete menu item is gated on `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}`. This PR computes `canDelete` from prom-rule-based abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) specifically so delete works in the list view where 'we have removed all requests to the ruler API', but in that context `rulerRule` is always `undefined`, so the item never renders even when `grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed` is true. The delete flow itself does not need the ruler rule — `RuleActionsButtons.V2` implements `handleDelete` as `() => showDeleteModal(identifier, groupIdentifier)`, which only uses the identifier. Net effect: users with delete permission cannot delete Grafana rules from the new list view (the updated GrafanaGroupLoader test even codifies this by expecting only 4 menu items with no Delete). Either drop the `rulerRule` requirement from the render guard or pass the identifier through instead.

findings.title: Silence menu item is shown in the list view but clicking it does nothing
findings.body: The silence drawer is only rendered when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is truthy: `{rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer && (<SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer rulerRule={rule} .../>)}`. In the new list view only `promRule` is supplied (ruler API calls were removed), so `rule` is undefined. Meanwhile `AlertRuleMenu` now shows the 'Silence notifications' item based on prom-rule-based `canSilence`, and `handleSilence` sets `showSilenceDrawer(true)` — but no drawer ever mounts. The user clicks the menu item and nothing happens. Either gate the silence menu item on the presence of a ruler rule, or make the drawer work from the prom rule data.

findings.title: Refactor of useAllAlertRuleAbilities drops the federated-rule-group immutability check
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (still used by existing components such as the old list's RuleActionsButtons via `useAlertRuleAbility`) previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated groups as immutable (no edit/delete). It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false;` with a TODO, and the `isFederatedRuleGroup` import was removed. As a result, rules in federated Mimir rule groups (groups with `source_tenants`) are no longer marked immutable on this code path, so Edit/Delete buttons can be shown for rules that must not be modified through Grafana. Restore the federated check for the CombinedRule-based path or thread the group's `source_tenants` into `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`.

findings.title: ModifyExport ability for Grafana prom rules excludes recording rules, removing Export from the list view
findings.body: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `[AlertRuleAction.ModifyExport]: [isAlertingRule, exportAllowed]` uses `prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)`, which is false for recording rules. The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` (`isGrafanaRulerRule`), which is true for both alerting and recording rules. In the list view (no ruler rule available), `canExport` therefore becomes false for Grafana-managed recording rules and the Export menu item disappears, whereas previously recording rules could be exported from the list. The same `isAlertingRule` gating on Pause/Restore also diverges from the old semantics (Grafana recording rules support pausing). Use a check that includes recording rules where the action legitimately applies to them.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries the returnTo parameter
findings.body: The previous implementation built the rule link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`; the new `GrafanaRuleListItem` drops the `returnTo` parameter. Users navigating from the list to a rule's detail page will lose the 'return to previous' context, so going back from the detail view no longer returns them to their filtered list position. If this was not an intentional product change, restore the `returnTo` query parameter.

findings.title: Stale comment and variable name still reference ruler rule preloading
findings.body: The comment above the cache-preload block still says 'This is not mandatory to preload ruler rules, but it improves the UX / Because the user waits a bit longer for the initial load but doesn't need to wait for each group to be loaded', and the variable is still named `cacheAndRulerPreload`, but the `alertRuleApi.util.prefetch('getGrafanaRulerGroup', ...)` call was removed in this PR. The comment now describes behavior the code no longer has and is misleading to future readers; update the comment and rename the variable to reflect that only the Prometheus groups cache is populated.
